whyWrongByChoice.E: PTHrP secretion causes hypercalcemia, not the presynaptic neuromuscular defect of LEMS.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman with newly diagnosed small cell lung cancer presents with confusion, malaise, and a seizure. Laboratory studies show a serum sodium of 118 mEq/L, low serum osmolality, and urine that is inappropriately concentrated. Which of the following mechanisms best explains her findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibodies against the Hu antigen on neurons and tumor cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic production of adrenocorticotropic hormone by the tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ectopic production of antidiuretic hormone by the tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tumor secretion of calcitriol acting on the intestinal mucosa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tumor secretion of parathyroid hormone-related protein

explanation.summary: Hyponatremia with low serum osmolality and concentrated urine in small cell lung cancer indicates SIADH from ectopic ADH production.
explanation.whyCorrect: The syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) results from ectopic, unregulated ADH production by the tumor, and small cell lung cancer is by far the most commonly associated cancer. Excess ADH increases water reabsorption in the collecting ducts, producing dilutional hyponatremia (Na <135 mEq/L), hypo-osmolality (<275 mOsm/kg), and urine that is less dilute than expected (>100 mOsm/kg), with neurologic symptoms such as seizures and decreased consciousness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-Hu antibodies cause limbic encephalitis, a neurologic syndrome, not an electrolyte disturbance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ectopic ACTH causes Cushing syndrome (hypercortisolism), which does not produce hyponatremia with concentrated urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Calcitriol secretion causes hypercalcemia (seen with lymphoma), not hyponatremia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PTHrP secretion causes hypercalcemia with low phosphate, not the hyponatremic picture described.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with small cell lung cancer develops central obesity, a rounded plethoric face, a dorsocervical fat pad, and new hyperglycemia. His serum cortisol is markedly elevated. Which of the following best explains the underlying mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoantibodies directed against the adrenal cortical cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic secretion of an ACTH-like substance by the tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ectopic secretion of antidiuretic hormone by the tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primary adrenal cortical adenoma independent of the lung tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tumor secretion of parathyroid hormone-related protein

explanation.summary: Paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome is caused by tumor secretion of an ACTH-like substance, most commonly by small cell lung cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cushing syndrome from high cortisol produces a dorsocervical fat pad (buffalo hump), moon facies, and hyperglycemia. Although most cases have other causes, a paraneoplastic subset is caused by small cell lung cancer secreting a substance so similar to ACTH that it stimulates cortisol production by the adrenal gland. This ectopic secretion is unresponsive to normal feedback inhibition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoantibodies against adrenal cells would reduce, not increase, cortisol and are not the paraneoplastic mechanism described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ectopic ADH causes SIADH with hyponatremia, not Cushing syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A primary adrenal adenoma is not a paraneoplastic syndrome and does not fit the setting of a known small cell lung cancer secreting an ACTH-like substance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PTHrP secretion causes hypercalcemia, not hypercortisolism.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with a heavy smoking history develops the subacute onset of short-term memory loss, seizures, personality changes, and olfactory hallucinations. MRI shows inflammation of the medial temporal lobes. Antibodies against which of the following are most characteristically implicated, and with which tumor is this syndrome most associated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anti-Hu antigen; small cell lung cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Presynaptic calcium channels; small cell lung cancer

choices.label: E
choices.text: PTHrP; squamous cell carcinoma of the lung

explanation.summary: Paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis presents with short-term memory loss and seizures, involves anti-Hu antibodies, and is most associated with small cell lung cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Limbic encephalitis is an immune-mediated inflammation of the limbic system with subacute short-term memory loss (a hallmark), seizures, personality changes, and olfactory/gustatory hallucinations. The most commonly associated cancer is small cell lung cancer, and antibodies against the neuronal antigen Hu (anti-Hu antibodies) play an important role.

whyWrongByChoice.B: NMDA receptor antibodies and ovarian teratoma define anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, which has a psychiatric prodrome and autonomic instability rather than isolated limbic memory loss.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Postsynaptic acetylcholine receptor antibodies with thymoma cause myasthenia gravis, a neuromuscular junction disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Presynaptic calcium channel antibodies cause Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (muscle weakness), not limbic encephalitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PTHrP from squamous cell carcinoma causes hypercalcemia, not an encephalitis.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man is noted to have the abrupt appearance of numerous gray-brown, flat-topped, velvety, stuck-on-appearing skin lesions across his trunk over a few weeks. Work-up is initiated for an underlying malignancy. This sign is most commonly associated with which cancer, and which secreted factor is thought to drive the lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma; transforming growth factor alpha

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovarian teratoma; antibodies against the NMDA receptor subunit

choices.label: C
choices.text: Small cell lung cancer; ectopic antidiuretic hormone secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung; parathyroid hormone-related protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thymoma; antibodies against the postsynaptic acetylcholine receptor

explanation.summary: The sign of Leser-Trelat is a sudden eruption of seborrheic keratoses associated with GI adenocarcinoma and driven by tumor secretion of TGF-alpha.
explanation.whyCorrect: The sign of Leser-Trelat is the sudden, explosive appearance of numerous seborrheic keratoses, which are gray-brown, flat-topped, velvety lesions with a stuck-on appearance. When they appear suddenly in large numbers, an underlying malignancy should be sought; the most commonly associated cancers involve the gastrointestinal tract. These tumors secrete transforming growth factor alpha, which stimulates keratinocytes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ovarian teratoma and NMDA receptor antibodies cause anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, not seborrheic keratoses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Small cell lung cancer and ADH cause SIADH, not seborrheic keratoses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Squamous cell carcinoma and PTHrP cause hypercalcemia, not the sign of Leser-Trelat.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thymoma and acetylcholine receptor antibodies cause myasthenia gravis, not a cutaneous eruption.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with lymphoma is found to have hypercalcemia. Unlike the more common paraneoplastic mechanism, laboratory studies show that both serum calcium and serum phosphate are elevated. Which of the following secreted substances best explains this finding?

explanation.summary: Calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia raises both calcium and phosphate and is seen primarily in lymphoma, distinguishing it from PTHrP-driven hypercalcemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although most paraneoplastic hypercalcemia is driven by PTHrP (which raises calcium but lowers phosphate), malignant tumors can also cause hypercalcemia by secreting calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D. Calcitriol ultimately increases both serum calcium and serum phosphate. This less common mechanism is seen primarily in patients with lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ACTH causes Cushing syndrome via cortisol, not hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ADH causes SIADH with hyponatremia, not hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PTHrP raises calcium but decreases phosphate, so it does not explain the elevated phosphate seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transforming growth factor alpha drives the sign of Leser-Trelat, not calcium elevation.

questions.stem: Paraneoplastic syndromes are groups of signs and symptoms that occur in patients with cancer but are not directly related to the growth of the tumor itself. Paraneoplastic syndromes are estimated to occur in up to what proportion of patients with cancer?

explanation.summary: Paraneoplastic syndromes occur in up to 10% of patients with cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Paraneoplastic syndromes result from some action of the tumor cells, such as secretion of hormone-like substances or stimulation of an aberrant immune response, rather than from the tumor mass itself. They are estimated to occur in up to 10% of patients with cancer, and they can affect just about every organ system, most commonly the nervous system, endocrine system, skin, and musculoskeletal system.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 25% overstates the frequency; paraneoplastic syndromes occur in up to about 10% of cancer patients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 40% is far higher than the estimated frequency of paraneoplastic syndromes in cancer patients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 60% is far higher than the estimated frequency; most cancer patients never develop a paraneoplastic syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 90% is the proportion of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy cases that are paraneoplastic, not the proportion of cancer patients with a paraneoplastic syndrome.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with no known history of cancer develops a subacute paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome that ultimately leads to the discovery of an occult malignancy. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which paraneoplastic syndromes of the nervous system almost exclusively arise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compression of peripheral nerves and spinal roots by the primary tumor mass

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct metastatic spread of tumor cells to the brain and spinal cord parenchyma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ectopic secretion of hormone-like substances by tumor cells into the blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immunologic cross-reactivity between nervous system components and tumor cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tumor secretion of growth factors that stimulate neuronal and glial proliferation

explanation.summary: Paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes almost exclusively result from immune responses to the malignancy that cross-react with components of the nervous system.
explanation.whyCorrect: Paraneoplastic syndromes affecting the nervous system almost exclusively result from immune responses to malignancy, that is, immunologic cross-reactivity between components of the nervous system and tumor cells. Because these syndromes are often detected before an actual cancer diagnosis, identifying a paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome is often the first clue to an underlying malignancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nerve compression by the tumor mass is a direct local effect of the tumor, not a remote paraneoplastic effect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Metastatic spread is a direct effect of the tumor and by definition is not a paraneoplastic syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ectopic hormone secretion is the mechanism of endocrine paraneoplastic syndromes such as Cushing syndrome, hypercalcemia, and SIADH, not neurologic ones.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor secretion of growth factors is the proposed mechanism for skin syndromes such as acanthosis nigricans and the sign of Leser-Trelat.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with fluctuating ptosis and muscle weakness that worsens with repetitive use is found to have an anterior mediastinal mass. The mass is resected. Histologic examination of the tumor is most likely to show a neoplasm derived from which of the following cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Germ cells from multiple embryonic layers

explanation.summary: Thymoma, the tumor most commonly associated with paraneoplastic myasthenia gravis, is a tumor in the thymus composed of thymic epithelial cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction, and in a subset of cases it is due to a tumor, most commonly thymoma. Thymoma is a tumor in the thymus composed of thymic epithelial cells. The immune response against an epitope expressed on thymoma cells cross-reacts with neuromuscular junction components sharing the same epitope.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tissue from multiple embryonic layers characterizes ovarian teratoma, the tumor associated with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphoma is associated with calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia, not with myasthenia gravis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neuroendocrine progenitor cells give rise to small cell lung cancer, which is associated with LEMS, not myasthenia gravis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Squamous cell carcinoma is the classic PTHrP-producing tumor causing hypercalcemia, not the tumor behind myasthenia gravis.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man is diagnosed with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome after presenting with proximal weakness that transiently improves with activity. He has no known malignancy. Approximately what proportion of patients with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome have small cell lung cancer?

explanation.summary: Between 40% and 62% of patients with LEMS have SCLC, so a patient presenting with LEMS should undergo a thorough evaluation for SCLC.
explanation.whyCorrect: LEMS is caused by autoantibodies against presynaptic calcium channels on motor neurons and, when paraneoplastic, is most commonly associated with small cell lung cancer. Between 40% and 62% of patients with LEMS have SCLC, whereas only about 2% to 3% of patients with SCLC have LEMS. Because such a large fraction of LEMS patients harbor SCLC, a patient presenting with LEMS should have a thorough evaluation for the cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Less than 1% grossly understates the association; roughly half of LEMS patients have SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 2% to 3% is the proportion of SCLC patients who have LEMS, the reverse relationship.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 10% to 15% understates the strong association between LEMS and SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: More than 90% overstates the association; not all LEMS is paraneoplastic.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history undergoes biopsy of a central lung mass discovered during evaluation of new proximal muscle weakness. Microscopy shows sheets of malignant cells with high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratios, finely dispersed chromatin, and nuclear molding. This tumor arises from which of the following?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lymphoid cells of the bronchial mucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primordial germ cells of the mediastinum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thymic epithelial cells of the mediastinum

explanation.summary: Small cell lung cancer is a smoking-associated tumor of neuroendocrine progenitor cells characterized by high N:C ratios, finely dispersed chromatin, and nuclear molding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Small cell lung cancer is an aggressive lung cancer associated with smoking that occurs predominantly in central airways and arises from neuroendocrine progenitor cells. Microscopy shows sheets of malignant cells with high nucleus:cytoplasmic (N:C) ratios, finely dispersed chromatin, and nuclear molding. SCLC is the tumor most commonly associated with paraneoplastic LEMS, limbic encephalitis, Cushing syndrome, and SIADH.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Squamous epithelium gives rise to squamous cell carcinoma of the lung, the classic PTHrP producer, which does not show these neuroendocrine features.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphoid cells give rise to lymphoma, which is associated with calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Germ cells give rise to ovarian teratomas, which contain tissue from multiple embryonic layers such as hair and teeth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thymic epithelial cells give rise to thymoma, an anterior mediastinal tumor associated with myasthenia gravis.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman is treated for anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. Pelvic imaging shows a cystic ovarian mass containing a tooth-like calcification and hair. Which of the following best characterizes this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Benign germ cell tumor containing tissue from multiple embryonic layers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epithelial tumor of the thymus expressing a cross-reactive epitope

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lymphoid malignancy secreting the active form of vitamin D

choices.label: D
choices.text: Malignant epithelial tumor secreting parathyroid hormone-related protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neuroendocrine tumor secreting an ACTH-like substance

explanation.summary: Mature cystic teratomas are the most common benign germ cell tumors and contain recognizable tissues such as hair or teeth from multiple embryonic layers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ovarian teratomas, more specifically mature cystic teratomas, are the most common benign germ cell tumors and typically occur in women of reproductive age. They are notable for containing tissue from multiple embryonic layers, so they contain recognizable tissues such as hair or teeth. Ovarian teratoma is the tumor most commonly associated with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A thymic epithelial tumor is a thymoma, associated with myasthenia gravis and located in the anterior mediastinum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Calcitriol secretion causing hypercalcemia is seen with lymphoma, not with an ovarian mass containing teeth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PTHrP-secreting epithelial tumors (squamous cell carcinomas and carcinomas of breast, ovary, kidney, bladder) cause hypercalcemia, not encephalitis, and do not contain hair and teeth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An ACTH-like substance is secreted by small cell lung cancer, causing Cushing syndrome.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman is brought to the hospital 4 days after a flu-like illness because of new paranoia, hallucinations, agitation, and insomnia. Her blood pressure and heart rate are stable, and she is fully alert. Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is suspected. Which of the following additional features is most likely to occur during this phase of the illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abnormal movements of the face and extremities

explanation.summary: Seizures are most common during the first, psychiatric-dominated phase of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis; catatonia, dyskinesia, and autonomic instability define the second phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: ANRE begins with headaches, fever, or flu-like symptoms, followed a few days later by a first phase dominated by psychiatric symptoms such as anxiety, agitation, paranoia, delusions, hallucinations, mania, cognitive deterioration, abnormal speech, and insomnia, along with behavior and personality changes. Seizures are most common during this first phase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abnormal movements of the face and extremities are neurologic features of the second phase, not the initial psychiatric phase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Catatonia and decreased consciousness characterize the second phase, which follows the first by about a week.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperthermia is part of the second-phase autonomic instability, along with tachycardia or bradycardia and hypotension or hypertension.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypoventilation is a manifestation of the autonomic instability of the second phase.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis has progressed to decreased consciousness, orofacial dyskinesias, and labile blood pressure. Imaging reveals an ovarian teratoma. In addition to supportive measures, which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and resection of the thymus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, and prompt tumor removal

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fluid restriction and pharmacologic correction of serum sodium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immunosuppression only if the symptoms become troublesome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intravenous fluids and correction of the serum calcium level

explanation.summary: ANRE can be lethal if untreated; immediate treatment includes steroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis, supportive measures, and removal of the offending tumor as soon as possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis itself can be lethal if not treated. Immediate treatment includes steroids, intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG), plasmapheresis, and supportive measures, and the offending tumor should be removed as soon as possible. This patient is in the second phase with autonomic instability, so urgent immunotherapy plus removal of the teratoma is indicated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Thymectomy is relevant to thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis, not to teratoma-associated ANRE.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluid restriction and sodium correction are the immediate management of SIADH, not of ANRE.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Deferring immunosuppression until symptoms are troublesome describes the approach to limbic encephalitis; ANRE requires immediate treatment because it can be lethal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IV fluids and calcium correction are the initial management of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman recovers from anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis after steroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis, and removal of an ovarian teratoma. Her family asks what to expect over the coming years. Which of the following is the most accurate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autonomic instability typically recurs every few months and requires repeated plasmapheresis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cognitive deficits, sleep disturbances, and behavioral abnormalities can persist for years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Muscle weakness that improves with repeated use is likely to develop over the next few years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progressive hypercalcemia commonly follows tumor removal and should be monitored with serial labs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recovery is complete once the tumor has been removed, and no further neurologic follow-up is needed

explanation.summary: Even with appropriate treatment of ANRE, cognitive deficits, sleep disturbances, and behavioral abnormalities can persist for years.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although immediate treatment with steroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis, supportive care, and tumor removal can prevent death from ANRE, the disorder leaves lasting effects. Even with appropriate treatment, cognitive deficits, sleep disturbances, and behavioral abnormalities can persist for years.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autonomic instability is a feature of the acute second phase, not a recurring long-term complication described for treated ANRE.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Weakness that improves with use is Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, associated with small cell lung cancer, not a sequela of ANRE.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypercalcemia is an endocrine paraneoplastic syndrome of PTHrP- or calcitriol-secreting tumors, not a consequence of ANRE.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor removal is essential, but recovery is not complete; long-term cognitive and behavioral sequelae are common.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old smoker with small cell lung cancer develops paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis. Which of the following groups of functions is regulated by the structures inflamed in this syndrome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balance, posture, and coordination of gait

choices.label: C
choices.text: Feeding, fleeing, fighting, feeling, and sex

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fine motor planning of the hands

explanation.summary: The limbic system is responsible for the five Fs: feeding, fleeing, fighting, feeling, and sex.
explanation.whyCorrect: Limbic encephalitis is inflammation of the structures that compose the limbic system, which is responsible for the famous five Fs: feeding, fleeing, fighting, feeling, and sex. This explains the typical presentation of short-term memory loss, personality changes, agitation, hallucinations, and sleep disturbance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Balance and gait coordination are cerebellar functions, not limbic functions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Breathing rate and blood pressure are brainstem autonomic functions; autonomic instability is a feature of ANRE rather than the limbic system's five Fs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fine motor planning is a function of the motor cortex, not the limbic system.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary sensory processing of vision, hearing, and touch is not a limbic function, although limbic encephalitis can produce olfactory and gustatory hallucinations.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with newly diagnosed small cell lung cancer has subacute short-term memory loss, personality changes, and olfactory hallucinations consistent with paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis. Which of the following is the most appropriate overall treatment approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, with surgical resection of the anterior mediastinal mass

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fluid restriction, with pharmacologic correction of the serum sodium over 24 hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intravenous fluids and bisphosphonates to lower the serum calcium before cancer treatment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasmapheresis, IVIG, and corticosteroids immediately, deferring any cancer-directed therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat the underlying cancer; add immunosuppression if symptoms are particularly troublesome

explanation.summary: In limbic encephalitis, treatment of the underlying cancer is of primary importance; immunosuppressive treatment may provide relief if symptoms are particularly troublesome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Limbic encephalitis is most commonly associated with SCLC, and its mechanism involves an autoimmune attack on limbic neurons in which anti-Hu antibodies play an important role. While treatment of the underlying cancer is of primary importance, if symptoms are particularly troublesome, immunosuppressive treatment may provide some relief.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and thymic resection relate to thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluid restriction and sodium correction are the immediate management of SIADH, not of limbic encephalitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IV fluids and calcium lowering are the initial management of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia; there is no hypercalcemia here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immediate steroids, IVIG, and plasmapheresis with tumor removal describe the treatment of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis; in limbic encephalitis cancer treatment is primary, not deferred.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung has a serum calcium of 14.6 mg/dL. Despite the markedly elevated calcium, the tumor continues to secrete a PTH-like substance. Which of the following best explains this persistence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anti-Hu antibodies block the calcium-sensing receptor on parathyroid cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic secretion is unresponsive to physiologic inhibiting signals

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypercalcemia stimulates further release of PTHrP by the tumor cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: The parathyroid glands are stimulated by the tumor to release PTH

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tumor cells convert vitamin D to calcitriol independent of calcium

explanation.summary: Ectopic hormone secretion by tumor cells lies outside the normal axis of hormonal control and does not respond to the feedback signals that shut off normal secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Normal hormone secretion is responsive to inhibiting signals: when serum calcium is low the parathyroids release PTH, and when calcium reaches normal levels PTH is no longer released. In hormone-related paraneoplastic syndromes the tumor cells make hormones on their own and do not respond to outside signals telling them to stop. This type of secretion is called ectopic, and because it is unresponsive to inhibiting signals, serum calcium can become markedly elevated while the tumor keeps secreting its PTH-like substance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-Hu antibodies mediate limbic encephalitis and have nothing to do with calcium regulation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypercalcemia does not stimulate PTHrP release; the point is that the tumor ignores the calcium level entirely rather than responding to it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The tumor does not stimulate the parathyroid glands; it secretes a PTH-like substance itself, and normal parathyroid secretion would be suppressed by the high calcium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Calcitriol production is a separate, less common mechanism of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia seen primarily in lymphoma, not in squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.stem: A routine metabolic panel is reviewed for a 60-year-old woman. Hypercalcemia is defined as a serum calcium concentration greater than which of the following values?

explanation.summary: Hypercalcemia is a serum calcium greater than 10.2 mg/dL.
explanation.whyCorrect: There are many causes of hypercalcemia, defined as a serum calcium greater than 10.2 mg/dL. Hypercalcemia is one of the most common paraneoplastic syndromes, and when it occurs as part of a paraneoplastic syndrome calcium levels can rise to dangerously high levels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 8.5 mg/dL lies within the normal range, near its lower end, and does not define hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 9.4 mg/dL is a normal serum calcium value.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 11.5 mg/dL is already hypercalcemic; the threshold defining hypercalcemia is lower, at 10.2 mg/dL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 12.8 mg/dL is well above the threshold and would represent significant hypercalcemia, not the defining cutoff.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman has a serum calcium of 10.9 mg/dL discovered on routine laboratory testing. She feels well and has no polyuria, constipation, bone pain, or neuropsychiatric symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her hypercalcemia?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic ACTH secretion by small cell lung cancer

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ectopic ADH secretion by small cell lung cancer

choices.label: E
choices.text: PTHrP secretion by an occult squamous cell carcinoma

explanation.summary: Asymptomatic hypercalcemia found on routine labs is most commonly due to primary hyperparathyroidism, whereas symptomatic hypercalcemia is most commonly due to malignancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: When a patient is found to have hypercalcemia on a routine laboratory assay but has no clinical signs or symptoms of hypercalcemia, the most common cause is primary hyperparathyroidism, in which something in the parathyroid gland itself is causing excess PTH secretion. When patients with hypercalcemia are symptomatic, the picture changes: the most common cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia is malignancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcitriol secretion by lymphoma is a much less common mechanism of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia and is not the most likely explanation for incidental asymptomatic hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ectopic ACTH causes Cushing syndrome with hypercortisolism, not hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ectopic ADH causes SIADH with hyponatremia, not hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PTHrP-mediated malignant hypercalcemia is the most common cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia, but this patient is asymptomatic with mild elevation.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck presents with confusion, vomiting, and lethargy. His serum calcium is 15.8 mg/dL. Markedly elevated calcium at this level places him at greatest risk for which of the following?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Muscle weakness that improves with use

explanation.summary: Markedly elevated calcium levels can cause irregular heart rhythms, and severe hypercalcemia can also lead to confusion, dementia, and coma.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to the classic stones, bones, groans, and psychiatric overtones, markedly elevated calcium levels can cause irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmia). Severe hypercalcemia can also lead to confusion, dementia, and coma, which is why managing the calcium level is the first priority in paraneoplastic hypercalcemia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Digital clubbing is a feature of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy, not a complication of hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypoventilation is a feature of the autonomic instability of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, not of hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Weakness that improves with use is Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome; hypercalcemia causes muscle weakness but not this use-dependent pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Velvety axillary hyperpigmentation is acanthosis nigricans, a skin paraneoplastic syndrome associated with gastric adenocarcinoma.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman with no known history of cancer presents with lethargy, confusion, and polyuria. Her serum calcium is 16.1 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin immunosuppressive therapy for a presumed autoimmune cause

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the serum calcium level before searching for the cause

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain a bone marrow biopsy to evaluate for lymphoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform whole-body imaging before any calcium-lowering therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restrict fluids until the cause is identified

explanation.summary: In dangerously elevated paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, managing the calcium level is the first priority; the search for the cause can proceed once the patient is stable.
explanation.whyCorrect: When hypercalcemia occurs as part of a paraneoplastic syndrome, calcium levels can increase to dangerously high levels. In these cases managing the calcium level is the first priority, since severe hypercalcemia can cause arrhythmia, confusion, dementia, and coma. A search for the cause can be undertaken once the patient is stable.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hypercalcemia is a hormone-mediated (PTHrP or calcitriol) syndrome, not an immune-mediated one, so immunosuppression has no role.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Evaluation for a specific malignancy such as lymphoma comes after the calcium is controlled and the patient is stable.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Delaying calcium-lowering therapy in favor of imaging risks arrhythmia and coma; the cause is sought once the patient is stable.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fluid restriction is the management of SIADH; hypercalcemia is treated with IV fluids, and withholding fluids would worsen dehydration.

questions.stem: Tumors that secrete parathyroid hormone-related protein include carcinomas of the lung, head and neck, breast, ovary, bladder, and kidney. Carcinomas are derived from which of the following types of tissue?

explanation.summary: Carcinomas are malignant tumors derived from epithelial tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cancers most commonly responsible for PTHrP production are carcinomas: squamous cell carcinoma of the lung and head and neck, as well as carcinomas of the breast, ovaries, bladder, and kidneys. Carcinomas, by definition, are malignancies of epithelial origin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Germ cell tissue gives rise to tumors such as ovarian teratoma, which is linked to anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymphoid tissue gives rise to lymphomas, which are associated with calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia rather than PTHrP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesenchymal connective tissue gives rise to sarcomas, not carcinomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neural tissue does not give rise to carcinomas.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man who smokes one pack of cigarettes daily is evaluated for shortness of breath and fever. He reports muscle weakness, constipation, fatigue, and feeling less mentally sharp. Chest x-ray shows a left lower lobe pneumonia and a 5-cm left upper lobe mass, and routine laboratory studies reveal an elevated serum calcium. In addition to antibiotics, which of the following is the most appropriate initial management of his hypercalcemia?

explanation.summary: Initial management of symptomatic paraneoplastic hypercalcemia from a suspected squamous cell lung carcinoma is administration of intravenous fluids.
explanation.whyCorrect: This patient's tobacco use, lung mass, and hypercalcemia with stones-bones-groans-psychiatric-overtones symptoms suggest squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with hypercalcemia from ectopic production of a PTH-like substance. He is admitted, antibiotics are started for the pneumonia, and IV fluids are administered as initial management of the hypercalcemia. Once the pneumonia is treated, the lung mass can be addressed more thoroughly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcitriol raises serum calcium and phosphate and is itself a cause of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia in lymphoma; giving it would worsen the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Steroids and IVIG are immediate treatments for anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, an immune-mediated syndrome, not for hormone-mediated hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluid restriction is the immediate management of SIADH-related hyponatremia, and it would worsen the dehydration of hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasmapheresis is used in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, not in paraneoplastic hypercalcemia.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with small cell lung cancer is found to have a serum sodium of 121 mEq/L with serum osmolality of 260 mOsm/kg and urine osmolality of 420 mOsm/kg. He is mildly confused. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin with tumor removal

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fluid restriction with pharmacologic correction of the serum sodium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immunosuppressive therapy directed at pathogenic neuronal antibodies

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intravenous fluids to expand the intravascular volume and lower calcium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation alone until the underlying tumor has been fully treated

explanation.summary: Immediate management of SIADH centers on correcting the serum sodium, mainly through fluid restriction and pharmacologic intervention, while definitive treatment addresses the underlying tumor.
explanation.whyCorrect: This patient has SIADH from ectopic ADH production by SCLC, with hyponatremia, hypo-osmolality (<275 mOsm/kg), and urine that is less dilute than expected (>100 mOsm/kg). The immediate management of SIADH is centered on correcting serum sodium levels, mainly through fluid restriction and pharmacologic intervention. As with all the paraneoplastic syndromes, the optimal treatment addresses the underlying tumor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Steroids and IVIG treat immune-mediated anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, not hormone-mediated SIADH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunosuppression targeting neuronal antibodies is used for troublesome limbic encephalitis; SIADH is caused by ectopic ADH, not antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IV fluids are the initial management of hypercalcemia; in SIADH, excess water is the problem, so fluids are restricted rather than given.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SIADH is a paraneoplastic syndrome that requires specific, urgent treatment; the hyponatremia cannot simply be observed until the tumor is treated.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman with small cell lung cancer develops paraneoplastic SIADH. Excess, unregulated ADH released by the tumor produces her hyponatremia through which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased sodium absorption from the gastrointestinal tract

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dilution of the serum together with increased sodium excretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased free-water excretion by the collecting ducts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased water reabsorption with reduced urinary sodium excretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Shift of sodium from the serum into cells

explanation.summary: Excess ADH causes hyponatremia by a dilutional effect in the serum and by increasing sodium excretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: ADH normally stimulates reabsorption of water in the collecting ducts of the kidney under tight physiologic feedback control. In paraneoplastic SIADH, the tumor releases ADH in an unregulated fashion, and this excess ADH causes hyponatremia (serum sodium <135 mEq/L) through a dilutional effect in the serum and by increasing sodium excretion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SIADH is a renal water-handling problem; it does not involve decreased gastrointestinal sodium absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ADH causes water reabsorption in the collecting ducts, the opposite of free-water excretion; increased free-water excretion would raise, not lower, serum sodium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ADH does increase water reabsorption, but sodium excretion is increased, not reduced, in SIADH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hyponatremia in SIADH is not due to sodium moving into cells; it results from water retention and sodium loss in the urine.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with small cell lung cancer is evaluated for several new problems over the course of his illness. Which of the following syndromes, if present, is most likely attributable to a tumor other than his small cell lung cancer?

explanation.summary: SCLC is associated with LEMS, limbic encephalitis, Cushing syndrome, and SIADH; paraneoplastic myasthenia gravis is most commonly associated with thymoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Small cell lung cancer is associated with multiple paraneoplastic syndromes, including Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, limbic encephalitis, Cushing syndrome, and SIADH. Myasthenia gravis, by contrast, is a neuromuscular junction disorder caused by antibodies against postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors, and when paraneoplastic it is most commonly associated with thymoma, so it would point to a separate tumor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome is most commonly due to SCLC secreting an ACTH-like substance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: LEMS is most commonly associated with SCLC through cross-reactivity between tumor epitopes and presynaptic calcium channels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Limbic encephalitis with anti-Hu antibodies is most commonly associated with SCLC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SCLC is by far the most common cancer associated with paraneoplastic SIADH.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy with obesity and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus has thickened, velvety, brown plaques on the back of his neck. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for his skin finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Association with obesity and diabetes rather than malignancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic secretion of an ACTH-like substance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Growth factor secretion by an occult gastric adenocarcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transforming growth factor alpha secretion by a GI tumor

explanation.summary: Most cases of acanthosis nigricans are associated with obesity or diabetes; only about 20% are related to an underlying tumor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acanthosis nigricans is thickened, black or brown, velvety hyperpigmentation most commonly on the neck and axilla. Most cases are associated with conditions such as obesity or diabetes. An estimated 20% of cases are related to an underlying tumor, most commonly gastric adenocarcinoma, but in an obese adolescent with diabetes the non-paraneoplastic association is far more likely.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ectopic ACTH secretion causes Cushing syndrome with buffalo hump and moon facies, not velvety hyperpigmentation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Growth factor secretion by gastric adenocarcinoma is the proposed mechanism of paraneoplastic acanthosis nigricans, which accounts for only about 20% of cases and would be unlikely in an obese diabetic teenager.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune cross-reactivity is the mechanism of paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes, not of acanthosis nigricans.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TGF-alpha secretion by gastrointestinal tumors is the mechanism proposed for the sign of Leser-Trelat (seborrheic keratoses), not acanthosis nigricans.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man is seen for a skin examination. Which of the following features of seborrheic keratoses would most strongly warrant a search for an underlying malignancy?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Slow appearance of a few lesions over many years

explanation.summary: Seborrheic keratoses are common in older adults and normally appear slowly; their sudden, explosive appearance in large numbers (the sign of Leser-Trelat) warrants a search for malignancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Seborrheic keratoses are gray-brown, flat-topped, velvety lesions with a stuck-on appearance that are commonly seen in middle-aged and elderly patients and typically appear slowly over time. When they appear suddenly and in large numbers, a search for an underlying malignancy, most commonly of the gastrointestinal tract, is warranted; this is the sign of Leser-Trelat.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A stuck-on appearance is characteristic of ordinary seborrheic keratoses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A flat-topped, velvety texture is a standard feature of seborrheic keratoses regardless of cause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gray-brown color is the normal appearance of any seborrheic keratosis and does not indicate malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Slow development of a few lesions over years is the typical benign pattern in older adults.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old woman with lung adenocarcinoma has digital clubbing, bilateral knee effusions, and pain in her wrists and ankles. Radiographs of the tibiae and fibulae show new bone formation along the shafts. Which of the following best describes the underlying skeletal process?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition within the synovial membrane and cartilage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erosive autoimmune synovitis with marginal joint erosions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Osteolytic destruction of cortical bone by metastatic deposits along the shafts

choices.label: D
choices.text: PTHrP-mediated osteoclast activation with diffuse cortical bone resorption

choices.label: E
choices.text: Subperiosteal bone formation and periostosis of tubular bones

explanation.summary: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy results from abnormal skin proliferation and subperiosteal bone formation along the phalanges, with periostosis and periostitis of tubular bones.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is a syndrome of digital clubbing, joint swelling with synovial effusions, and joint pain, especially in the large joints; 90% of cases are paraneoplastic and lung cancer of any type is the most commonly associated malignancy. Its mechanism is abnormal skin proliferation and subperiosteal bone formation along the shafts of the phalanges, with periostosis (excessive bone formation) and periostitis (inflammation of the periosteum) of tubular bones.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Synovial calcium deposition is not the described mechanism; the process is excessive bone formation beneath the periosteum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy produces synovial effusions from periosteal bone changes, not an erosive autoimmune synovitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metastatic bone destruction is a direct effect of tumor spread, not a paraneoplastic syndrome, and would not produce new periosteal bone along long-bone shafts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PTHrP causes hypercalcemia; it is not the mechanism of the clubbing and periosteal changes of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presents with hemoptysis and weight loss, and imaging reveals a spiculated lung mass. Setting his individual case aside, which of the following cancers is the leading cause of cancer-related death in both men and women in the United States?

explanation.summary: Lung cancer is the number one cause of cancer mortality in both sexes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although breast (women) and prostate (men) cancers have higher incidence, lung cancer has a poor prognosis and causes the most cancer deaths in both men and women. Many of these deaths are preventable by avoiding tobacco smoke.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in women but is the second most common cause of cancer death in women, not the first.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Colorectal cancer is a common cancer but ranks below lung cancer as a cause of cancer death.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pancreatic cancer is uncommon and highly lethal, but its total number of deaths is far below that of lung cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men but has a relatively good prognosis and is not the leading cause of cancer death.

questions.stem: In the United States, both the incidence of and mortality from cervical cancer decreased by more than 60% between 1955 and 1992. Which of the following interventions is most responsible for this dramatic decline?

explanation.summary: Cervical cancer rates fell largely because of Pap smear screening.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Papanicolaou (Pap) test, introduced in the 1950s, allows cytologic detection of precancerous cervical lesions before invasive cancer develops. Its widespread use is credited with the >60% decline in cervical cancer incidence and mortality in the US during this period.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Low-dose chest CT is used for lung cancer screening and is unrelated to cervical cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fecal occult blood testing screens for colorectal cancer, not cervical cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Colonoscopy screens for colorectal cancer and has no role in cervical cancer prevention.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mammography is a screening test for breast cancer, not cervical cancer.

questions.stem: A healthy 45-year-old man with no personal or family history of cancer or cancer syndromes presents to establish care and asks about cancer screening. At what age is initiation of colorectal cancer screening routinely recommended for an average-risk individual such as this patient?

explanation.summary: Average-risk colorectal cancer screening begins at age 45.
explanation.whyCorrect: For healthy individuals without a family history or cancer syndrome, colonoscopy screening is recommended beginning at age 45 and is repeated every 10 years. Colonoscopy is the gold standard because it visualizes the colon and removes polyps before they can progress to cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Age 21 is when average-risk women typically begin Pap smear (cervical cancer) screening, not colorectal screening.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Age 30 is when high-risk BRCA1/2 carriers may begin breast MRI screening, not colorectal screening.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Age 40 applies to patients with a family history of colorectal adenocarcinoma (or 10 years before the affected relative's onset), not to average-risk patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Because most cancers occur in patients over 55 years of age, beginning routine screening at 65 would miss many preventable cancers.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man who worked for decades installing insulation and demolishing old buildings presents with dyspnea and chest pain. Imaging shows diffuse pleural thickening, and pleural biopsy reveals a malignant tumor. Occupational exposure to which of the following is most likely responsible for his cancer?

explanation.summary: Asbestos exposure from construction materials causes mesothelioma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Asbestos, encountered in construction materials, is the classic occupational carcinogen linked to mesothelioma, a pleural-based malignancy. This patient's demolition and insulation work is a typical high-exposure history.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Benzene, found in printing, paint, and light oil, is linked to acute myeloid leukemia, not mesothelioma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radon, encountered in underground mines and some homes, is linked to lung cancer rather than pleural mesothelioma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ultraviolet radiation causes skin cancers such as melanoma and squamous cell carcinoma, not mesothelioma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vinyl chloride, used in refrigerants and adhesives, is linked to hepatic angiosarcoma.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man who has worked in a printing and paint manufacturing plant for many years presents with fatigue and easy bruising. His blood counts show pancytopenia, and bone marrow evaluation confirms acute myeloid leukemia. Chronic occupational exposure to which of the following agents is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Benzene exposure is linked to acute myeloid leukemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Benzene is encountered in printing, paint, and light oil and is a well-recognized occupational carcinogen linked to acute myeloid leukemia. This patient's plant work fits the classic exposure history.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aromatic amines are not the occupational agent emphasized here; the printing and paint setting points specifically to benzene and acute myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Asbestos, from construction materials, is linked to mesothelioma, not leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radon, from underground mines and some residences, is linked to lung cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vinyl chloride, from refrigerants and adhesives, is linked to hepatic angiosarcoma.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man who worked for years manufacturing polyvinyl chloride products presents with right upper quadrant pain. Imaging reveals a vascular hepatic tumor, and biopsy confirms a malignant tumor of endothelial origin in the liver. Occupational exposure to which of the following is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Vinyl chloride exposure causes hepatic angiosarcoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vinyl chloride, used in refrigerants and adhesives, is the occupational carcinogen linked to hepatic angiosarcoma, a malignant vascular (endothelial) tumor of the liver. This patient's PVC manufacturing work is the classic exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aflatoxin is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma, not the endothelial hepatic angiosarcoma described, and is not the occupational agent emphasized in this brick.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Asbestos is linked to mesothelioma, a pleural tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Benzene is linked to acute myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radon is linked to lung cancer, not a hepatic vascular tumor.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman is diagnosed with luminal (hormone receptor-positive) breast cancer. In counseling her, you note that increased lifetime estrogen exposure is an important risk factor for this cancer. Which of the following features in her history most likely increased her estrogen exposure and her breast cancer risk?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having given birth to five children

explanation.summary: Early menarche increases lifetime estrogen exposure and breast cancer risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen stimulates growth and epithelial proliferation in luminal breast cancer. Risk factors that increase estrogen exposure include menarche before age 12, delayed first childbirth after 30 or nulliparity, supplemental estrogen, and postmenopausal obesity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Postmenopausal obesity, not being underweight, is the estrogen-related risk factor for breast cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Early menopause shortens the reproductive window and reduces lifetime estrogen exposure, lowering risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An early first full-term pregnancy is protective, whereas delaying first childbirth past age 30 raises risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Higher parity (more pregnancies) reduces lifetime estrogen exposure because progesterone counterbalances estrogen during pregnancy.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with a long history of chronic gastritis undergoes endoscopy. Biopsies show gastric adenocarcinoma in one region and a mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lymphoma in another. Which of the following infectious agents is most likely causally related to both of these neoplasms?

explanation.summary: H. pylori is causally linked to gastric carcinoma and MALT lymphoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although viruses cause most infection-related cancers, Helicobacter pylori is a well-researched bacterial example that is causally related to both gastric carcinoma and MALT lymphoma. Infectious agents cause roughly 15% of cancers worldwide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epstein-Barr virus is not the agent emphasized here; the gastric carcinoma plus MALT lymphoma combination points specifically to H. pylori.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatitis viruses may cause hepatocellular carcinoma, not the gastric tumors described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Human herpesvirus 8 is associated with Kaposi sarcoma, not gastric cancer or MALT lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HPV causes cervical cancer, not gastric carcinoma or MALT lymphoma.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man who drinks alcohol heavily and smokes a pack of cigarettes daily presents with progressive dysphagia and weight loss. Endoscopy reveals an esophageal mass, and biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma. His combination of exposures is best described as having what effect on his cancer risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alcohol and tobacco act synergistically to increase risk

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alcohol protects against the carcinogenic effect of tobacco

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neither exposure affects the risk of esophageal cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only alcohol contributes; tobacco is not a risk factor for this cancer

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only tobacco contributes; alcohol is not a risk factor for this cancer

explanation.summary: Alcohol and tobacco act synergistically to raise the risk of aerodigestive cancers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Excessive alcohol increases the risk of cancers of the mouth, larynx, and esophagus, and when the patient is also a smoker, the risk is synergistically increased. Both exposures are independent risk factors whose combined effect is greater than additive.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Alcohol does not protect against tobacco; it amplifies the carcinogenic risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both alcohol and tobacco clearly increase esophageal cancer risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tobacco is a major risk factor for esophageal cancer, so alcohol is not the only contributor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alcohol is itself an established risk factor for esophageal cancer, so tobacco is not the only contributor.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man with a strong family history of colon cancer undergoes colonoscopy, which reveals hundreds of adenomatous polyps carpeting the colon. He is told that without intervention his lifetime risk of colorectal adenocarcinoma approaches 100%. A germline mutation in which of the following genes is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Familial adenomatous polyposis is caused by a germline APC mutation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Familial adenomatosis polyposis syndrome carries a nearly 100% chance of colorectal adenocarcinoma and is due to a germline mutation in the APC tumor suppressor gene. The hundreds of adenomas and near-certain cancer risk are classic.

whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA1 mutations predispose to breast and ovarian carcinoma, not colonic polyposis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NF1 mutations cause neurofibromatosis 1, characterized by neurofibromas and cafe-au-lait macules.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RB1 mutations cause retinoblastoma tumor predisposition syndrome, not colonic polyposis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TP53 germline mutations cause Li-Fraumeni syndrome, associated with breast cancer and other tumors.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with a family history of breast and ovarian cancer diagnosed before age 50 is found to carry a germline BRCA1 mutation. She is counseled about intensified screening, including breast MRI before age 30 and consideration of prophylactic mastectomy. The BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes normally function to prevent cancer by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Encoding a growth-factor receptor tyrosine kinase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maintaining DNA repair and genomic stability

choices.label: E
choices.text: Producing estrogen to regulate epithelial growth

explanation.summary: BRCA1/2 are DNA-repair genes; their loss causes genomic instability and cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: BRCA1 and BRCA2 are important to DNA repair, and their absence creates genomic instability that can lead to cancer. Because carriers are high-risk, experts recommend MRI screening before age 30 and some choose prophylactic mastectomy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Although they repair DNA broadly, their described role is genomic stability, not selective repair of UV-damaged skin cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA1/2 are DNA-repair genes, not growth-factor receptor tyrosine kinases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: They do not detoxify chemical carcinogens; their role is genome maintenance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: BRCA genes do not produce estrogen; estrogen exposure is a separate risk factor for breast cancer.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy is evaluated for multiple flat, hyperpigmented (cafe-au-lait) skin macules and several soft cutaneous nodules that on biopsy are neurofibromas. He is diagnosed with an inherited tumor predisposition syndrome. A germline mutation in which of the following tumor suppressor genes is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is caused by inherited NF1 mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neurofibromatosis 1 is caused by inherited mutations in the NF1 tumor suppressor gene and manifests with cafe-au-lait macules and multiple neurofibromas, exactly as described in this child.

whyWrongByChoice.A: APC mutations cause familial adenomatous polyposis with colorectal adenocarcinoma, not neurofibromas.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA2 mutations predispose to breast and ovarian carcinoma, not neurofibromatosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RB1 mutations cause retinoblastoma, a childhood eye tumor, not cafe-au-lait macules and neurofibromas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TP53 mutations cause Li-Fraumeni syndrome, associated with breast and other cancers.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is diagnosed with thyroid cancer after a nodule is found on routine examination. She is frightened because she knows thyroid cancer is fairly common in women. Which of the following best explains why thyroid cancer, despite its relatively high incidence in women, does not appear on the list of cancers causing the most deaths in women?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is almost always rapidly fatal before it can be recorded

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is classified as a benign neoplasm rather than a cancer

choices.label: C
choices.text: It occurs almost exclusively in men rather than women

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its incidence is too low to register in national statistics

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its prognosis is so good that it is almost always curable

explanation.summary: Thyroid cancer is common but almost always curable, so it is absent from the cancer-death list.
explanation.whyCorrect: Each cancer type has its own prognosis, which is why the lists of the most common cancers and the cancers causing the most deaths look different. Thyroid cancer is fairly common, especially in women (about 5% of new female cases), but its prognosis is so good that it does not even make the list of cancers causing the most deaths in women.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rapid fatality describes pancreatic cancer, which is the opposite situation: uncommon but almost always rapidly fatal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Thyroid cancer is a true malignancy; it is its excellent prognosis, not its classification, that keeps it off the mortality list.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thyroid cancer is more common in women than in men.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thyroid cancer is fairly common, especially in women, and appears among the most frequently diagnosed cancers.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman with no family history of cancer drinks four to five alcoholic beverages nightly. She has no history of liver disease. She asks whether her drinking affects her risk of breast cancer. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which alcohol consumption increases breast cancer risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alcohol increases estrogen levels in the body

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alcohol induces cirrhosis, which secondarily transforms breast epithelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Alcohol interferes with the detection of microcalcifications on mammography

choices.label: D
choices.text: Alcohol is metabolized to a compound that mimics the DNA damage of UV light

choices.label: E
choices.text: Alcohol lowers progesterone, which removes protection during pregnancy

explanation.summary: Alcohol raises estrogen levels, which increases breast cancer risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond its effects on the mouth, larynx, esophagus, and liver, alcohol also increases estrogen levels in the body, which increases the risk of breast cancer. Estrogen is an important risk factor for luminal breast cancer because it stimulates growth and epithelial proliferation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Alcoholic cirrhosis predisposes to hepatocellular carcinoma, not breast cancer; the breast effect is hormonal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Alcohol does not impair mammographic detection; it raises risk through estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The breast cancer link is via increased estrogen exposure, not a UV-like DNA-damage mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone during pregnancy counterbalances estrogen, but alcohol does not act by lowering progesterone.

questions.stem: A healthy 19-year-old woman who recently became sexually active asks her physician when she should begin cervical cancer screening. She has no known risk factors. According to general guidelines for average-risk patients, at what age are Pap smears typically initiated?

explanation.summary: Pap smear screening generally begins at age 21 in average-risk women.
explanation.whyCorrect: Recommendations for when to begin Pap smears and how frequently vary by expert guidelines, but they generally begin at the age of 21 years in average-risk patients. The Pap smear collects cells from the cervical surface with a swab for cytopathologic examination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Screening is not started at 16; guidelines generally begin at 21 for average-risk women.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Age 18 is earlier than the generally recommended starting age of 21.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Age 25 is later than the general starting age for Pap smears in average-risk patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Age 30 is the age before which BRCA1/2 carriers begin MRI screening for breast cancer, not the Pap smear starting age.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman undergoes routine cervical cancer screening. The cytopathologist reports clusters of atypical cells with increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, nuclear enlargement, and nuclear membrane irregularity, interpreted as a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reassurance, because these are normal squamous cells

explanation.summary: An HSIL result on Pap smear prompts high-risk HPV testing and consideration of further sampling or treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: An abnormal Pap smear prompts additional investigation and possible intervention before a cancer can develop or progress. The presence of HSIL on cytopathology would prompt high-risk HPV testing and consideration of additional sampling or treatment, depending on the patient's age and risk status.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HSIL is a precancerous lesion evaluated with HPV testing and additional sampling, not immediate removal of the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HSIL cells are atypical, not normal; normal squamous cells have small nuclei and abundant cytoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Routine-interval repeat cytology would miss the opportunity to intervene on a precancerous lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mammography screens for breast cancer and is unrelated to an abnormal cervical cytology result.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man who has never smoked is diagnosed with lung cancer. He worked for 30 years in underground mines and has lived for decades in a home in a region known for high natural levels of a radioactive gas. Occupational and residential exposure to which of the following is most likely responsible for his cancer?

explanation.summary: Radon exposure in underground mines and some homes is linked to lung cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Radon, encountered in underground mines and some residential properties, is an occupational and environmental carcinogen linked to lung cancer. The combination of mining work and residential exposure in a nonsmoker points to radon.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aflatoxin is not the occupational carcinogen described; the mining and residential radioactive-gas history points to radon.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Asbestos, from construction materials, is linked to mesothelioma, a pleural tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Benzene, from printing, paint, and light oil, is linked to acute myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vinyl chloride, from refrigerants and adhesives, is linked to hepatic angiosarcoma.

questions.stem: A public health physician is planning a cervical cancer prevention program for a low-income country. She reviews global data on cervical cancer distribution. Which of the following statements about the worldwide epidemiology of cervical cancer is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Approximately 80% of cervical cancer occurs in developing countries

choices.label: B
choices.text: HPV PCR testing has replaced Pap smears in most developing countries

choices.label: C
choices.text: Incidence and mortality have fallen more than 60% worldwide since 1955

choices.label: D
choices.text: Roughly 7 in 100,000 women in developing countries develop cervical cancer each year

choices.label: E
choices.text: The majority of cervical cancer cases occur in the United States

explanation.summary: Eighty percent of cervical cancer occurs in developing countries with limited Pap smear access.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although cervical cancer has become rare in the United States (about 7 in 100,000 US women in 2014, roughly 0.007% of the female population), it remains a scourge worldwide: 80% of cervical cancer occurs in developing countries. This is an area of global health that can be definitively addressed by increasing access to Pap smears in these countries.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HPV PCR may replace Pap smears in the future, but only in countries with access to this technology; developing countries have limited access even to Pap smears.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The more than 60% decline in incidence and mortality from 1955 to 1992 occurred in the United States, not worldwide.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 7 in 100,000 figure describes US women in 2014, not developing countries, where the burden is far higher.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cervical cancer is rare in the United States; most cases occur outside it, in developing countries.

questions.stem: A health ministry in a rapidly urbanizing developing country notes that colorectal cancer has become far more frequent over the past several decades as its cities have adopted Western lifestyles and diets. Which of the following best describes the worldwide trend in colorectal cancer incidence since the 1900s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreasing, because of falling rates of Helicobacter pylori infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreasing, because of widespread adoption of fecal occult blood testing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increasing, because of rising rates of HPV infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increasing, in parallel with economic development and longer life expectancy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unchanged, because it is driven almost entirely by hereditary mutations

explanation.summary: Colorectal cancer incidence has risen worldwide with economic development and Western diets.
explanation.whyCorrect: The incidence of colorectal cancer has increased worldwide since the 1900s in parallel with economic development and longer life expectancy. This trend has been especially true in developing countries such as urban China, where Western lifestyles and diets have been adopted; as of 2010, 5%-6% of individuals worldwide are expected to develop colorectal cancer in their lifetimes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: H. pylori is linked to gastric carcinoma and MALT lymphoma, not colorectal cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The worldwide trend is upward; the recent decrease (2%-4%) was seen in the United States between 2003 and 2012.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HPV causes cervical cancer; it is not the driver of colorectal cancer trends.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Most colorectal cancer is sporadic and influenced by environmental factors such as diet; incidence has changed, not stayed flat.

questions.stem: An epidemiologist reviews United States cancer registry data and finds that the incidence of colorectal cancer decreased significantly, by 2%-4%, between 2003 and 2012 across all major ethnic groups and in both men and women. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this decline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Declining prevalence of germline APC mutations in the United States population

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased awareness of colorectal cancer screening aided by national campaigns

choices.label: C
choices.text: Introduction of the Pap smear as a screening test in the 1950s

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced dietary intake of refined carbohydrates and processed meat across the population

choices.label: E
choices.text: Widespread eradication of Helicobacter pylori through antibiotic treatment programs

explanation.summary: The recent US decline in colorectal cancer incidence is attributed to increased screening awareness.
explanation.whyCorrect: From 2003 to 2012 the incidence of colorectal cancer in the United States decreased by 2%-4% in all major ethnic groups and both sexes. This may be due to increased awareness of colorectal cancer screening, aided by campaigns such as Screen for Life, a national project of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); colonoscopy removes polyps before they can become cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Germline APC mutations cause familial adenomatous polyposis; their prevalence does not change over a decade and does not explain population trends.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Pap smear is a cervical cancer screening tool and explains the fall in cervical, not colorectal, cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Excess refined carbohydrates, fat, and processed red meat raise colorectal risk, but a national dietary reversal is not the explanation given for the decline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: H. pylori is causally related to gastric carcinoma and MALT lymphoma, not colorectal cancer.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man declines colonoscopy and asks whether a fecal occult blood test alone would be adequate to catch colon cancer early. Which of the following best describes the principal limitation of the fecal occult blood test as a screening tool?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood in the stool is typically present only in more advanced cancers, not in polyps

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cannot detect occult bleeding that originates in the lower gastrointestinal tract

choices.label: C
choices.text: It detects only bleeding that arises from tumors in the upper gastrointestinal tract

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is expensive and technically difficult to perform outside a referral center

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires full bowel preparation and procedural sedation for each test

explanation.summary: Fecal occult blood testing has limited utility for early cancer because polyps and early cancers usually do not bleed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blood in the stool in any adult is suspicious for occult bleeding from a tumor in the lower gastrointestinal tract, which is the basis for the fecal occult blood test, a simple, cheap method of detecting blood in the stool. However, because blood in the stool is typically only present in more advanced colon cancers (and not in polyps), the utility of this test in detecting early cancer is limited.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The test is specifically designed to detect occult bleeding from tumors in the lower gastrointestinal tract.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The test detects blood from lower gastrointestinal tumors; the limitation is that early lesions do not bleed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The fecal occult blood test is described as simple and cheap; its limitation is sensitivity for early lesions, not cost.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bowel preparation and a scope are features of colonoscopy, not of the stool-based occult blood test.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman undergoes screening colonoscopy, during which a pedunculated polyp is removed. Microscopic examination shows crowded, neoplastic glands with no invasion beyond the basement membrane into the lamina propria. Which of the following best describes this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenoma, a precursor lesion removed before progression to adenocarcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hyperplastic mucosa without neoplastic change or malignant potential

choices.label: C
choices.text: Invasive adenocarcinoma through the basement membrane requiring colectomy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metastatic carcinoma seeded from a primary breast tumor elsewhere

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma involving the colon wall

explanation.summary: Crowded neoplastic glands without invasion past the basement membrane define a colon adenoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Colon adenomas, including pedunculated examples, can be removed during colonoscopy before the neoplasms progress to adenocarcinoma. Microscopically, crowded neoplastic glands are seen in the absence of invasion beyond the basement membrane and into the lamina propria, which is why colonoscopy is the gold-standard screening test.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The glands are described as neoplastic and crowded, which excludes a purely hyperplastic, non-neoplastic process.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Invasive adenocarcinoma would show neoplastic glands invading beyond the basement membrane, which is absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A metastasis would invade the colon wall; a polyp of neoplastic glands confined above the basement membrane is a primary adenoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MALT lymphoma is a lymphoid neoplasm associated with H. pylori in the stomach, not a glandular polyp of the colon.
